query: Use drug "Segesterone acetate" as a target reference and drug "Bexarotene" as an indication reference. Consider only other solid drugs carrying an approved group label, with positive target overlap with the first, a nonempty indication difference from the second, and a target set unequal to the first. Rank by no weighted sum: a drug is dominated only when another eligible drug is no worse on all three objectives and better on at least one. The objectives are more shared targets with the first reference, more distinct indications not recorded for the second, and fewer total targets. Return the entire nondominated set; keep all exact ties. Use distinct target proteins and distinct indication diseases; carrier, enzyme and transporter edges are not target edges.

Take the target proteins of drug "Oxtriphylline" as the first position and those of drug "Estrone" as the second position in ordered protein pairs. A disease is eligible only if it is not an indication of drug "Captodiame". Filter the first position to proteins explicitly expression-present, with no expression-absent record, in anatomy "smooth muscle tissue". Return diseases associated with both members of exactly 3 qualifying pairs; a protein cannot fill both positions. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

For drugs "Binimetinib" and "Aldesleukin", consider ordered protein pairs (x,y), where x is a target of the first drug and y a target of the second. Exclude diseases indicated for drug "Trifluoperazine". Require x to have an expression-present edge to anatomy "decidua" and no expression-absent edge to that same anatomy. Which diseases have exactly 2 such pairs with x and y different and both proteins associated with the disease? Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

Compare the complete target sets of drugs "Labetalol" and "Iloperidone". Their exclusive targets are proteins targeted by one of these drugs but not the other. Find pathways linked by protein-pathway interacts-with edges to exactly 2 first-drug-exclusive targets and at least 1 second-drug-exclusive target, and to none of the proteins shared by their target sets. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

For proteins "ELMO1" and "PCOLCE2", first delete all target proteins of drug "N-Formylmethionine" and their incident edges from the PPI graph; never delete the endpoints. Treat the surviving graph as undirected and find its shortest routes between the endpoints. Report every interior node occurring on at least one such route that is recorded expression-present and not expression-absent in anatomy "artery". The expression test filters answers after route computation. If the retained endpoints are disconnected, the answer is empty. Duplicate or reverse PPI records count as one undirected edge.

Use drugs "CRx-139", "Estrone", and "2-(5-HYDROXY-NAPHTHALEN-1-YL)-1,3-BENZOOXAZOL-6-OL" as ordered target sources. Count ordered triples only when the three selected proteins are pairwise different, all are associated with the same disease, and the first and third interact with the second through PPI edges but not directly with each other. Which diseases have exactly 2 valid triples? PPI edges are undirected. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

I need the trade-off frontier relative to drug "Homosalate" for target overlap and drug "PRLX 93936" for new indications. Start from solid, approved-labeled drugs other than these references, requiring at least one shared target with the first and at least one indication missing from the second; discard exact target-set copies of the first. A candidate is dominated when another remaining drug has at least its shared-target count, at least its new-indication count, and at most its total target count, improving at least one count strictly. Return all candidates not dominated, retaining ties. Use distinct target proteins and distinct indication diseases; carrier, enzyme and transporter edges are not target edges.

In the undirected PPI graph, connect proteins "PANX1" and "CFAP161" while avoiding the targets of drug "ENMD-1198". Remove those target nodes and their incident edges first, retaining either endpoint if it is a target. Recompute shortest routes on this smaller graph. Return all internal nodes on any of its tied shortest routes that have expression-present and no expression-absent evidence in anatomy "nasopharynx". If the retained endpoints are disconnected, the answer is empty. Duplicate or reverse PPI records count as one undirected edge.

Using drugs "Cyproheptadine" and "Ergotamine", split their targets into first-only, second-only, and shared proteins. Return pathways having exactly 1 link to distinct first-only proteins, at least 2 to distinct second-only proteins, and zero to shared proteins. These exclusive targets are defined by target edges; pathway links must be protein-pathway interacts-with edges. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

Compare drugs "Droxicam" and "Tizanidine" through disease-associated target proteins, excluding all indication diseases of drug "Ziprasidone". In anatomy "tongue", the first drug's witness must have expression-present but no expression-absent evidence. Keep the second drug's targets unfiltered by expression. Find diseases with exactly 2 ordered protein pairs of these witnesses, requiring different proteins in the two positions. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

For drugs "PD-168393" and "Zanubrutinib", I need pathways supported by exclusive targets from both sides: exactly 1 distinct target unique to the first drug and at least 2 unique to the second. Reject a pathway if even one target shared by the two drugs has an interacts-with edge to it. Use target edges for the drug sets and protein-pathway interacts-with edges for support. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

Look for diseases admitting exactly 1 ordered triple of witnesses for drugs "Nadroparin", "AT9283", and "Norethisterone", respectively. A witness is a target protein associated with that disease. Require three different proteins, a PPI edge between positions one and two and between positions two and three, and no PPI edge between positions one and three. Treat PPI as undirected. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

For drugs "Pramipexole", "Ulipristal", and "Hydrocortisone valerate", use the drug order as the three positions in ordered triples of target proteins. Return diseases that admit exactly 1 triple of different associated proteins forming an open PPI chain: the first-second and second-third edges must exist, while the first-third edge must not exist. Every protein in a triple must have an associated-with edge to the returned disease. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity. Treat PPI edges as undirected.

Consider drugs "Talampanel", "Testosterone", and "Phenolphthalein" in that order. Find diseases supported by exactly 2 ordered triples (x,y,z), choosing one target from each drug. All three proteins must be different and associated with the same disease. In the undirected protein-protein interaction graph, x must be directly linked to y and y directly linked to z, but x and z must have no direct PPI link. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

I want disease records supported by exactly 2 ordered protein pairs from drugs "CRA_8696" then "(R)-Rolipram". Omit any indication disease of drug "Formoterol". For anatomy "smooth muscle tissue", the first protein must be recorded as expression-present and not expression-absent; the second protein has no expression restriction. Each pair uses one target per drug, two different proteins, and associated-with edges from both proteins to the same disease. Return all matching node IDs. Count distinct proteins and assignments; repeated edge records add no multiplicity.

For proteins "SLC25A21" and "SAP30L", enumerate the distinct shortest routes in the undirected PPI graph conceptually. Which non-endpoint proteins occur on a strict majority of these routes but are not unavoidable? Here strict majority means more than half, and not unavoidable means absent from at least one shortest route. Count routes by their ordered node sequences, not by edge-record multiplicity.

Find the interior proteins traversed by more than half but fewer than all shortest routes from protein "TBC1D28" to protein "IDI1" in the undirected PPI graph. Include all ties meeting both strict bounds. Treat duplicate and reverse PPI records as a single edge, and distinguish routes by their node sequences. Exclude the endpoints.

Find protein nodes on shortest routes between "XKR8" and "PITPNM2" after removing every target of drug "Baricitinib" from the undirected PPI graph, except that the two endpoint proteins are always retained. Perform this removal before computing distances. From the interior nodes lying on at least one shortest route in the remaining graph, return those explicitly expression-present in anatomy "artery" with no expression-absent record there. If the retained endpoints are disconnected, the answer is empty. Duplicate or reverse PPI records count as one undirected edge.

In the undirected PPI graph, consider all shortest routes between proteins "GATA6" and "SLITRK5". Return interior protein nodes lying on more than half, but not all, of those routes. A route is a distinct sequence of node IDs from the first endpoint to the second; duplicate and reverse edge records do not create extra routes. Exactly half does not qualify, and neither endpoint may be returned.

Compare drug candidates against "Theophylline" for targets and "Alefacept" for indications. Eligible candidates are solid drugs whose group labels include approved (additional labels are allowed), excluding both reference drugs, with at least one target shared with the first reference, at least one indication absent from the second reference, and a complete target set different from the first reference. Keep candidates that are not dominated: another eligible drug dominates one if it shares at least as many targets with the first reference, has at least as many indication diseases absent from the second, and has no more total targets, with at least one of these three comparisons strict. Return every nondominated drug, including equal-score ties. Use distinct target proteins and distinct indication diseases; carrier, enzyme and transporter edges are not target edges.
